title: Shavur Malka
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Bava Batra 115b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.115b.5), the title refers to Shmuel in one version and Rabbah in another.

[Pesachim 54a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.54a.16) gives Shmuel or Rava. Hyman separately describes Shavur Malka, the Persian king, as always speaking with Shmuel, as in [Berakhot 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.56a.1), [Moed Katan 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.26a.9-10), [Bava Metzia 119a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.119a.5) and [Sanhedrin 98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.98a.14).[^2]

notes.text: The rabbinic nickname and the Persian king are separate uses of the same designation. No particular historical ruler or identity merger is added.

[Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3270&lang=en) lists the rabbinic nickname. The linked Bava Batra and Pesachim explicitly ask who the nickname denotes in their respective versions. The linked Berakhot, Moed Katan and Sanhedrin instead present Shavur Malka speaking to Shmuel. The closing Bava Metzia notice gives only the title in that exchange.
